perspectives.name: discovery-weak-signals
observations: Centrus announced a definitive multi-year HALEU supply contract with Antares on 2026-09-17, with deliveries commencing before decade-end and customer prepayments supporting capacity expansion.

A separate Radiant agreement announced 2026-09-09 also adds a domestic HALEU customer and prepayments, strengthening the signal that advanced-reactor demand is converting into contracted backlog rather than remaining only prospective.
Centrus priced a $500 million equity-and-warrant financing on 2026-09-09, adding expansion capital but also introducing dilution and warrant-overhang risk.

perspectives.name: expectations-execution
observations: The July 2026 DOE contract finalized a $900 million award supporting commercial-scale HALEU capacity, while Centrus reported completion of an additional 900 kg of HALEU UF6 ahead of schedule.
Recent Antares, Radiant and X-energy agreements include prepayments that can help finance build-out, providing a customer-funded execution mechanism alongside federal support.
Commercial-scale delivery remains a future execution obligation; signed supply agreements and financing do not by themselves prove achieved large-scale production economics or schedule performance.

risks: Equity and warrant issuance creates dilution/overhang risk.
Customer delivery schedules extend toward the end of the decade and remain execution-dependent.
Federal policy and contracting remain material dependencies.
unknowns: Exact aggregate contracted HALEU volumes and backlog economics were not established in the sources used.
Final commercial-scale unit costs and realized margins remain unverified.
Timing and exercise behavior of the September warrants remains uncertain.
